BiblicalUsage: Folly is the opposite of wisdom, and the Preacher gives his heart to know it: madness and folly, and the difference between them. He tries wine and wisdom and folly together, and finds the same end waiting for them all. The word appears only in Ecclesiastes, and it carries the book's verdict on a life without God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe folly is not stupidity; it is wisdom without God, and the Preacher proves it by trying everything. He had the wealth and the wisdom to test it all, and his verdict stands. My position is that folly ends where it began — in vanity — and only the fear of God gives wisdom its meaning.
